standards.residual_gap: Compatibility surfaces are legacy/non-standard behavior; no explicit reusable security control was curated in the bounded pass.
standards.title: Compatibility

standards.residual_gap: Malformed streams fail, but decompression-bomb and resource-amplification limits are not explicitly defined as reusable security controls.
standards.title: Compression

standards.residual_gap: Console formatting and debugging behavior were assessed; privacy or diagnostic leakage concerns do not yield an explicit reusable access control.
standards.title: Console

standards.residual_gap: RFC 6265bis supplies much of the normative cookie security model; follow that dependency for SameSite, Domain, Path, and prefix details.
standards.title: Cookie Store API

standards.residual_gap: Trusted Types attribute integration is cataloged; DOM is cross-cutting and downstream HTML sinks and mutation consumers remain dependency-heavy.
standards.title: DOM

standards.residual_gap: Decoder-specific malformed-sequence behavior remains distributed across individual encoding algorithms.
standards.title: Encoding

standards.residual_gap: CORS, filtering, headers, redirects, and CORP are covered initially; mixed content, CSP, SRI, PNA, ORB, cache partitioning, and authentication dependencies require separate standards review.
standards.title: Fetch

standards.residual_gap: User-selected file permission lifetime and revocation are supplied by integrating specifications and user-agent policy.
standards.title: File System

standards.residual_gap: Keyboard lock integration and platform UI details are not fully enumerated in this initial catalog.
standards.title: Fullscreen API

standards.residual_gap: HTML is very large; origin, sandbox, COOP/COEP, canvas, activation, and meta CSP are covered, while navigation, messaging, workers, storage, embeds, forms, and many feature-specific guards need targeted follow-up.
standards.title: HTML

standards.residual_gap: Infra defines generic data structures and algorithms; none were promoted without an explicit security-boundary consequence.
standards.title: Infra

standards.residual_gap: Context-specific sniffing tables and Fetch's X-Content-Type-Options integration need joint review for a concrete API.
standards.title: MIME Sniffing

standards.residual_gap: Permission is cataloged; frequency, deceptive content, and platform anti-abuse policy are largely user-agent concerns rather than explicit reusable controls here.
standards.title: Notifications API

standards.residual_gap: Legacy CSS/selector compatibility behavior did not expose an explicit reusable security mechanism.
standards.title: Quirks Mode

standards.residual_gap: Quota and clearing are implementation-defined; storage partitioning can evolve beyond the current origin tuple.
standards.title: Storage

standards.residual_gap: Backpressure, cancellation, and error propagation are generic resource-management primitives unless an integrating API establishes a security boundary.
standards.title: Streams

standards.residual_gap: The standard is an internal testing surface and was classified testing-only, not a production API security-control source.
standards.title: Test Utils

standards.residual_gap: Most validation errors are non-fatal; each integrating API must decide which URL conditions are security-fatal.
standards.title: URL

standards.residual_gap: Regexp-group restriction is informative integration guidance, not a built-in complexity bound or policy language.
standards.title: URL Pattern

standards.residual_gap: Exposure and exception redaction are covered; type conversion and binding exceptions remain generic unless tied to a concrete API boundary.
standards.title: Web IDL

standards.residual_gap: Server-side Origin validation, authentication, TLS, extensions, and protocol message authorization require RFC and application review.
standards.title: WebSockets

standards.residual_gap: XHR delegates most network security semantics to Fetch; use the Fetch catalog for complete CORS and response-filtering behavior.
standards.title: XMLHttpRequest
